title: Little Office of S. Anthony of Padua

introductoryNotes.text: Courtesy of Michael Martin, www.preces-latinae.org — transcription of the original text.

blocks.source: Ad Matutinum
blocks.english: At Matins

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth will announce Thy praise.

blocks.source: Ad Completorium
blocks.english: At Compline

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos, Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thy wrath from us.

blocks.source: Ad Horas Omnes
blocks.english: At all the Hours

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adiutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my aid.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adiuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: ℣. Gloria Patri, et Filio, et Spiritui Sancto.
blocks.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, and to the Holy Spirit.

blocks.source: ℟. Sicut erat in principio, et nunc, et semper, et in saecula saeculorum. Alleluia.
blocks.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, and ever shall be, world without end. Alleluia.

blocks.source: A Septuagesima usque ad Pascha, loco Alleluia, dicitur: Laus tibi, Domine, Rex aeternae gloriae.
blocks.english: During Lent until Easter, instead of the alleluia the following is said: Praise to Thee, O Lord, King of everlasting glory.

blocks.source: While in the world’s delights he was wont to stray, he learned to shun the snare of vice and rougher paths obey; to passions and to pleasures false he ceased to yield his heart, and Anthony resolved to God his whole to set apart.
blocks.english: Dum mundi in deliciis solet ambulare inventus, capita vitiis aspera vitare, et sensualitatibus pravis indulgere, se statuit Antonius Deo devovere.

blocks.source: Aurelianam primitus regulam professus, in arduis virtutibus miros fecit gressus: vitam deinde pauperum elegit Minorum, quem movit constans Martyrum mors Marochiorum.
blocks.english: Having first professed the rule of Aurelian, he made wondrous progress in the heights of virtue: then chose the life of the poor among the Friars Minor, moved by the constant deaths of the Martyrs of Morocco.

blocks.source: Antonii sub nomine zelo Dei ductus, praeclaros sanctimoniae mox produxit fructus: Diebus dum et noctibus precibus vacabat, Et austeris operibus carnem macerabat.
blocks.english: Under the name of Anthony, led by zeal for God, he soon bore noble fruits of sanctity: by day and night he gave himself to prayer, and with austere works he mortified the flesh.

blocks.source: Praeconio deinde inclytus Verbi Dei factus, id successive caelitus est talentum nactus; ut doceret impios semitam virtutis, et revocaret devios in vitam salutis.
blocks.english: Renowed then as a herald of God’s holy Word, he received successively a talent from heaven; to teach the wicked the path of virtue, and to call back the straying to the life of salvation.

blocks.source: In Scripturae codicibus ita versabatur, praeripere quod omnibus palmam videbatur: sacrorum inde codicum arca est vocatus, recte Doctorum omnium gemma nuncupatus.
blocks.english: In the books of Scripture he was so versed that he seemed to outstrip all and win the palm: therefore he was called the ark of sacred writings, rightly named the gem of all Doctors.

blocks.source: Impugnator acerrimus fit haereticorum, terror et pavor maximus turbae paganorum: eliminator criminum morumque corrector, salus periclitantium, clientum protector.
blocks.english: A Most ardent assailant of heretics he became, greatest terror and dread of the pagan crowd: banisher of crimes, corrector of morals, salvation of those in danger, protector of his clients.

blocks.source: Multis tandem laboribus fractus aegrotabat, suamque circumstantibus mortem nuntiabat: istam dum Fratres populo volunt occultare, inventa mox in oppido coepit divulgare.
blocks.english: Worn at last by many labors he fell ill, and foretold to those around him that his death was near: while the Brethren wished to hide it from the people, news of it quickly spread throughout the town.

blocks.source: Ant. O Proles Hispaniae, pavor infidelium, nova lux Italiae, nobile depositum urbis Paduanae: fer, Antoni, gratiae Christi patrocinium, ne prolapsis veniae tempus breve creditum defluat inane.
blocks.english: Ant. O Offspring of Spain, terror of the unbelievers, new light of Italy, noble treasure of the city of Padua: grant us, Anthony, the patronage of Christ’s grace, that the brief time given for pardon may not slip by in vain.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis, beate Antoni.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, blessed Anthony.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Ecclesiam tuam, Deus, Beati Antonii Confessoris tui deprecatio votiva laetificet, ut spiritualibus semper muniatur auxiliis, et gaudiis perfrui mereatur aeternis. Per Dominum Iesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate Spiritus Sancti, Deus per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: May Thy Church, O God, be gladdened by the devout prayers of Blessed Anthony, Thy Confessor, so that it may always be protected by spiritual help and deserve to enjoy eternal joys. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God forever and ever. Amen.
